notes: The base revision was not readable in this checkout; all `base` citations are supported by the unified diff hunks and the structural diff's recorded source ranges for the removed symbol, not by reading base files.
No test files appear in the diff, so whether existing tests encode the old n+1 eviction behaviour could not be determined from the inputs.

claims.text: `evict_oldest` took a count `n` and returned nothing; it looped over the inclusive range `0..=n`, so it attempted n+1 pops rather than n, and it silently did nothing on an empty queue because the `if let Some(..)` arm had no else branch.
`Cache::put` called `evict_oldest(overflow + 1)` when the map was at or over `max_entries`, so the number of entries actually dropped per insertion was one more than the argument it passed.
The struct's `max_entries` field was not exposed by any accessor of that name; the only capacity-related public reader was `free_slots`, which reports remaining room rather than the configured bound.

citations.item: pub fn kvstore::cache::Cache::evict(&mut self, usize) -> usize

claims.text: `evict` iterates `0..n` and `match`es on `pop_front()`, incrementing a `removed` counter for each entry it deletes from the map and breaking out of the loop on `None`; it returns that count.
The doc comment on the method now states the return contract explicitly: "Evict the `n` oldest entries, returning how many were removed."
A new `capacity()` accessor returns the `max_entries` field, documented as "The configured maximum number of entries."
`put` is unchanged apart from the callee name: it still computes `overflow` and requests `overflow + 1` evictions, now via `evict`.
Because the public method `evict_oldest` disappeared, cargo-semver-checks records an `inherent_method_missing` lint at major level and the package requires a major version bump.
`kvstore/src/cache.rs` no longer contains `evict_oldest`; it now contains `evict` and `capacity` instead.
The call edge from `Cache::put` to `evict_oldest` was removed and replaced by a call edge from `Cache::put` to `evict`; `put` remains the only in-crate caller of the eviction routine.

The structural diff treats `evict` as a likely rename of `evict_oldest` (confidence 0.75) on the basis of the same file and overlapping source range, rather than as an unrelated new symbol — the removed symbol spanned lines 40-47 and the new one spans lines 40-53.
`capacity` is genuinely new rather than renamed: it appears in the API delta's added list and has no counterpart in the removed list.
`handle_request` in `kvstore/src/api.rs` reaches the changed code through a call to `Cache::put` and could be affected; it is the only entry in the impact set, and it is ranked as public API.

The impact set is bounded reverse reachability at one hop over calls and imports, and its own caveat notes that a listed symbol depends on something the change altered without being known to be broken by it.

The number of entries dropped per `put` changed silently: the argument `overflow + 1` is unchanged, but the callee now removes at most that many instead of one more than that. Anything that relied on the old over-eviction — a test asserting cache length after inserting past the bound, or a hit-rate expectation — will now see a different result even though the call site looks identical in the diff.

The new return value is not consumed at the only call site: `put` discards the count `evict` returns, so a short eviction (queue exhausted before `n` pops) is invisible to `put` and the subsequent `push_back`/`insert` proceeds regardless.

`evict` removes from `order` and `map` in step, but `put` pushes to `order` and inserts into `map` unconditionally; a reviewer should confirm the two structures stay in agreement when a key is re-inserted, since the eviction count is now derived from `order` pops rather than from `map` removals succeeding.

citations.item: pub fn kvstore::cache::Cache::evict(&mut self, usize) -> usize

claims.text: Because the rename is a breaking API change requiring a major bump, external callers of `evict_oldest` must be migrated, and the version bump should be checked — the structural diff records no package version changes in this commit.

`capacity` and the pre-existing `free_slots` are now adjacent public readers with different meanings — the configured bound versus `max_entries.saturating_sub(map.len())` — which is a plausible confusion point for callers.

output.summary: This change replaces `Cache::evict_oldest(n)` with `Cache::evict(n) -> usize`, which stops when the queue is empty and reports how many entries it actually removed, and adds a `Cache::capacity()` accessor for the configured maximum. The old method iterated `0..=n`, removing one entry more than requested; the new one iterates `0..n` and breaks on an empty queue. `Cache::put` is updated to call the new method. Removing the public `evict_oldest` method makes this a major semver bump for the `kvstore` package.
